items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: Oh yes, I was a very good friend to Buddy.

ctx.x: You said you knew Buddy Petit?

Oh yes, I was a very good friend to Buddy. I think I recall telling Bill Russell an incident about Buddy and I. I used to play on this boat they call the Susquehanna. I don't know if you can recall that. You probably weren't nowhere around New Orleans. I read the name. You read the name? Yeah. Well the Susquehanna would leave Spanish Fort and go across the lake and it would dock over in, what's the name of the little town over there? Vanderville? Northern. Covington? Covington. And the doctor, it would dock there…
Do you remember anything about his style? Like you know, was he a high note man?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: Right, right, over there at his home.

ctx.x: Well, the capital. You owned the capital. Right, but however the boat here was the Sesquahanna. Yeah, I heard. That's on Lake Pontchintrain. That was with Bigfoot, Bill, Phillips, when I was just beginning.
Yeah, you tell me about that and meeting Buddy Petit and all those things.
Right, right, over there at his home.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: That's why I made a great friendship over there with one of the greatest trumpet players that I have ever heard, and that was Buddy Petit.

ctx.x: Oh yes, I've heard about that.

We would go on the boat at a certain time and start playing music. We'd play until the Susquehanna landed over in Mandeville. Then we would get off and go around the town until time for the boat to leave then. That's why I made a great friendship over there with one of the greatest trumpet players that I have ever heard, and that was Buddy Petit. Buddy lived in Covington and Mandeville, all those places are right close together, so I would frequent him quite a lot. Then like I said, Mr. How did he sound? How did…
People tell us he was wonderful on the blues like Careless Love, but was he good on other things too, everything? Or what style did he have?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: And we'd sit down and talk with Buddy. And I'd ask him questions about his horn.

ctx.x: Well, what was it like on the other side? Beautiful.

I can remember the trees and the green shrubbery. A few homes. Beautiful homes sitting in these, under these great big trees. Of course, you had the slum area over there. Well, now I wouldn't say slum. I hate to use it. Yeah. But, for instance, Buddy B.T. lived in the great trumpet players about 25, 30 years ahead of time. He lived in the little one room shack and he took a vacuum to me. And every time I would go to the dock, I'd try to see how fast I could get off of that. And we'd sit down and talk with Buddy.…
One of the things I was trying to get in there from a slant and vicular way as a country.
